A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSBL framework and retain the three principal experimental settings. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments using a KuaiRand-based recommender simulator, a cuisine-generation simulator and simulated multi-turn conversations.

after.justification: v2 retains original results for those settings and adds an experimental comparison with tabular Q-learning in Appendix F.1.

M1.justification: Recursive training, policy and feedback modification, the inverse-propensity macro objective, and top-down inference remain unchanged. The hierarchical-prior interpretation and explicit inference pseudocode do not introduce a different learning procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds a small synthetic finite-horizon item-selection environment with two contexts and ten items. The three principal settings remain; renaming the text-generation simulator as a conversational recommender system does not add another task.

E2.justification: v2 introduces tabular Q-learning as an evaluated comparator in Appendix F.1. It also removes the fixed Level-3 intervention baseline from the three-level aggregate and subgroup comparisons: v1 Figures 6, 10 and 11 versus v2 Figures 4(b), 10 and 11. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 replaces the separate 2,000-user two-level training specification with a shared 1,500-user description. It changes the stated diversity measure from one minus normalized 3-gram repeats to normalized repeats, and replaces the graded activity-preference reward with an incompletely defined indicator. The new toy experiment compares episode requirements at matched expected reward. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new toy experiment analyzes sample efficiency relative to Q-learning as item-selection size varies. Existing ranking-size, micro-policy-noise, feature-noise and subgroup analyses remain, although several move to the appendix or receive revised results.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies five random seeds for the multi-turn and three-level aggregate results, adds error bars and shaded variability regions, and reports feature-noise results with plus/minus quantities. v1 already used five seeds elsewhere. The uncertainty measures are not clearly defined, and newly reported seed counts do not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Several result sets change substantially. Aggregate multi-turn MSBL reward changes from approximately 0.69 in v1 Figure 7(b) to 0.60 in v2 Figure 3(b); at feature noise 0.10, the reported reward changes from approximately 0.77 to 0.86. Three-level aggregate and subgroup results are revised, and Appendix F.1 adds Q-learning/MSBL episode ratios of roughly 10–62. These are revised or new results, not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3 and Appendix E add an explicit i.i.d. assumption, a PAC-Bayesian generalization argument, Gaussian KL-divergence and Mahalanobis-distance derivations, and illustrative sample-saving calculations of 98% and 88.2%. v1 contains the nested-policy definitions and objectives but no corresponding theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion newly present recursive construction of data-informed hierarchical priors for faster macro-level learning as a central contribution. v1 primarily claims reconciliation of feedback timescales through nested policies and objective selection. The underlying MSBL and long-term-optimization claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains that the proposed sample savings depend on the learned micro policy providing a prior closer to the long-term optimum, and qualifies savings by accounting for cheaper micro-level samples. It also treats principled extension to stateful policies as future work. Existing reward-tradeoff interpretations and concerns about unavailable public multi-scale datasets largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds GPU specifications, simulator-module and configuration descriptions, and the recommender dataset's 5,659-item count. Conversely, it removes the multi-turn experiment's 160,800-prompt and 293-user training counts and the explicit activity-preference payoff mapping. Most model hyperparameters and the code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to London and Sandler, McAllester, Zhang et al., and Zong et al., while removing Stray et al. It reframes the distinction from hierarchical reinforcement learning around data-informed priors, but retains the principal related-work categories and comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 merges motivation into the introduction, introduces an explicit contribution list, reverses the micro/macro learning exposition, reorders the experiments and reorganizes the appendices. The abstract, related-work discussion and conclusion are substantially rewritten, beyond the insertion of new scientific material.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v2 merges two- and three-level result displays, separates aggregate and subgroup conversation plots, moves robustness figures, converts the feature-noise graph into a table, and redraws several plots. It also adds prior, simulator-module and Q-learning comparison illustrations.

improvement.justification: The PAC-Bayesian motivation, toy Q-learning comparison and broader uncertainty reporting strengthen the rationale and supporting evidence. However, v2 removes training counts and the explicit activity-reward definition, while changing the diversity definition without explaining its relationship to the revised results. The PDFs do not resolve whether these reflect intended protocol revisions or documentation errors. Consequently, the gains cannot be weighed reliably against the resulting reproducibility and interpretation problems.
